summary.title: Vidu S1: A Real-Time Interactive Video Generation Model

setting_and_object.category: System / Model artifact (streaming autoregressive video-audio diffusion model plus inference stack)

details: Existing video generators are offline and one-shot: users cannot intervene during generation, speech is rarely an explicit control signal for future content, and long autoregressive rollouts drift or collapse.
Real-time interaction additionally demands an inference/serving stack fast enough to run on commodity GPUs.

Vidu S1: a causal, few-step autoregressive video+audio diffusion model for voice-controlled digital characters, where user speech (plus text instruction and a reference first frame) acts as a streaming conditioning sequence so content can be redirected at any moment.

Training crux: bidirectional video-audio teacher, then causal adaptation with a per-sample Bernoulli mix of Teacher Forcing (clean prefix) and Diffusion Forcing (noisy prefix), then distillation to few steps via DMD regularized by a phased-consistency (PCM) objective with a perceptual distance.

Inference crux: infinite-length sliding-window decoding with a persistent 'sink' reference context, RoPE applied after caching (repositioning), and TwinCache — a noisy history cache attended during intermediate denoising steps and a clean cache at the final step — decoupling temporal propagation from appearance refinement to curb error accumulation.
Single-person, single-shot clips from livestream/talking-head video plus film and TV footage; deduplication and prefiltering on frame rate, resolution, audio-visual integrity and sync.
Shot-boundary clipping into 3–60 s clips with cut points constrained away from mid-speech.

Joint filtering by expert models plus an omni (video-understanding) model over subject count, frame cleanliness (watermarks/subtitles), aesthetic/technical quality, NSFW safety, shot stability (static/slow motion to reduce drift), and interactivity.
Speech diarization with VAD and active-speaker detection labeling onscreen/offscreen/overlap (overlap clips discarded), plus a heuristic dropping low speech-energy vocalization segments.
Dual-granularity captions: full-clip captions and speech-aware chunk-level captions, with visual attributes from frames and acoustic attributes from audio only to reduce cross-modal hallucination.
TurboDiffusion-aligned worker-side stack with TurboServe as cluster serving reference.
SageAttention / SpargeAttention / Sparse-Linear Attention for attention acceleration; custom per-block W8A8 CUDA GEMM kernels (per-tensor and per-channel found outlier-sensitive).

Triton/CUDA kernel fusion (e.g., RMSNorm plus elementwise), CUDA Graph capture/replay for the repetitive short-kernel streaming pattern, and Ulysses-style context parallelism with all-to-all across GPUs.

Vidu-StreamBench (in-house, 500 samples): action instruction + reference first frame + audio clip, spanning styles, speaker attributes, emotions, scenarios; evaluated by pairwise A/B human preference.
HDTF as public reference with CSIM (identity), Sync-D (audio-visual sync), DOVER (perceptual quality).
Efficiency measured on RTX 5090 GPUs with a 3-step sampling configuration at 540p (960x540).
Open-source audio-driven avatar models: Wan2.2-S2V-14B, LiveAvatar, OmniAvatar-1.3B, Hallo3, StableAvatar-1.3B.

key_findings.finding: Vidu S1 attains the best reported quality on HDTF among compared avatar systems while being the only one that is both real-time and instruction-following.
Real-time streaming generation is achievable on a consumer GPU without sacrificing avatar quality.
key_findings.evidence: 540p (960x540) generation with a 3-step sampling configuration reaches average throughput of 42 FPS on RTX 5090, above the 30-FPS playback threshold, while retaining the HDTF identity/sync/quality scores; other real-time baselines report at most 25 FPS (HeyGen) or unspecified rates.

key_findings.finding: Explicit action-instruction control gives the largest human-preference advantage, particularly in subject controllability.
key_findings.evidence: Pairwise A/B tests on the 500-sample Vidu-StreamBench show consistent overall preference over HeyGen, LemonSlice and Kling Avatar 2.0, with a 100% preference rate on subject controllability against HeyGen and LemonSlice, plus gains in motion dynamics and audio-video synchronization; qualitative examples show the baseline failing to raise the head or produce a thumbs-up while Vidu S1 succeeds.

key_findings.finding: Stage-aware dual caching (TwinCache) plus a persistent reference sink enables indefinitely long streaming without drift or collapse at constant per-step latency.
key_findings.evidence: Attention is restricted to a fixed sliding window containing the persistent first-frame/first-state context, cached history and the current state; historical context uses a noisy cache during intermediate denoising steps (acting as an implicit low-pass prior that suppresses high-frequency artifact accumulation) and a clean cache at the final step to restore detail, with RoPE applied after caching so visible positions stay in the trained range.

key_findings.finding: Pure DMD distillation of the causal model is unstable, and phased-consistency regularization is needed for stable few-step autoregressive generation.
key_findings.evidence: The authors report that optimizing with the DMD objective alone frequently causes mode collapse manifesting as camera drift, content degeneration and temporal inconsistency; adding the PCM objective instantiated with a perceptual feature distance against an EMA student mitigates these effects.
